answer: Moshi adds Mimi, a semantic-acoustic neural audio codec, which encodes audio into discrete units amenable to language modeling [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion]. The system models audio tokens along with a text stream aligned on the audio frame rate [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 55, §Appendix C. Delayed text LM as a zero-shot streaming ASR and TTS]. The streaming design claims a theoretical latency of 160ms [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 26][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion].
